subject: English
topic: Reported Speech — Direct to Indirect Narration (Set W7)

questions.stem:
Convert to indirect speech:
He said, 'I am very happy today.'

options.option_text: He said that he is very happy today.
He said that he was very happy that day.
He told that he was very happy today.
He said that he had been very happy that day.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Key changes: (1) 'said' (no object) → 'said that' (no change in reporting verb). (2) 'am' → 'was' (tense backshift: simple present → simple past). (3) 'I' → 'he' (pronoun change). (4) 'today' → 'that day' (time expression change). Option A keeps 'today' and 'is' — wrong. Option C uses 'told' without an object — 'told that' is wrong; use 'told him that' or 'said that'.

questions.stem:
Convert to indirect speech:
She said to me, 'Do you like coffee?'

options.option_text: She asked me that I like coffee.
She told me whether I liked coffee.
She asked me whether I liked coffee.
She asked me did I like coffee.

questions.explanation: C is correct. For Yes/No questions: (1) Reporting verb 'said to' → 'asked'. (2) Use 'whether' or 'if' (no 'that' for questions). (3) Remove auxiliary inversion: 'do you like' → 'I liked'. (4) Tense backshift: 'like' → 'liked'. Option A uses 'that' (for questions, use whether/if). Option D keeps the inverted word order — wrong in indirect speech.

questions.stem:
Convert to indirect speech:
'Close the door,' he said to me.

options.option_text: He told me to close the door.
He said me to close the door.
He told me that close the door.
He said to me that I should close the door.

questions.explanation: A is correct. For commands/orders: (1) Reporting verb becomes 'told/ordered/asked + object + to + infinitive'. (2) Remove inverted commas and imperative structure. 'He told me to close the door.' Option B uses 'said me' — wrong; 'said' cannot take an indirect object without 'to'. Option C uses 'that close' — wrong; use infinitive form.

questions.stem:
Convert to indirect speech:
He said, 'I have completed the project.'

options.option_text: He said that he has completed the project.
He said that he completed the project.
He said that he have completed the project.
He said that he had completed the project.

questions.explanation: D is correct. Tense backshift: Present Perfect ('have completed') → Past Perfect ('had completed'). The backshift rule: when the reporting verb is past ('said'), all tenses in the direct speech shift one step back into the past. Present Perfect → Past Perfect is one of the most commonly tested shifts.

questions.stem:
Convert to indirect speech:
She said, 'We will visit the museum tomorrow.'

options.option_text: She said that they will visit the museum the next day.
She said that we would visit the museum tomorrow.
She said that they would visit the museum the next day.
She said that they shall visit the museum the following day.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Changes: (1) 'We' → 'they' (pronoun, third person). (2) 'will' → 'would' (tense backshift). (3) 'tomorrow' → 'the next day' / 'the following day' (time expression). Option A keeps 'will' — wrong. Option B keeps 'we' and 'tomorrow' — both wrong. Option D uses 'shall' — wrong backshift ('shall' would become 'should', not used here).

questions.stem:
Convert to indirect speech:
He asked me, 'Where do you live?'

options.option_text: He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me that where I lived.
He asked me where do I live.

questions.explanation: B is correct. For Wh-questions: (1) 'where' stays as connector (no 'that'). (2) Remove auxiliary inversion: 'where do you live' → 'where I lived'. (3) Pronoun 'you' → 'I'. (4) 'do live' → 'lived' (tense backshift + remove auxiliary). Options A and D keep the inverted order (did I / do I) — wrong in indirect speech.

questions.stem:
Convert to indirect speech:
'Please help me with the luggage,' she said to the porter.

options.option_text: She requested the porter to help her with the luggage.
She told the porter please to help her with the luggage.
She said to the porter that please help her with the luggage.
She ordered the porter to help her with the luggage.

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Please' signals a polite request → use 'requested + object + infinitive'. 'She requested the porter to help her with the luggage.' Note pronoun change: 'me' → 'her'. Option D uses 'ordered' — too forceful/wrong tone. Option B keeps 'please' in the indirect speech — wrong.

questions.stem:
Convert to indirect speech:
'Don't make noise,' the teacher said to the students.

options.option_text: The teacher told the students do not make noise.
The teacher asked the students not to make noise.
The teacher said to the students that don't make noise.
The teacher told the students not to make noise.

questions.explanation: D is correct. For negative commands: (1) Reporting verb = 'told'. (2) Structure = 'told + object + not to + infinitive'. 'The teacher told the students not to make noise.' Note: 'asked' (option B) also works for requests but 'told' is more appropriate for a teacher's instruction/command.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct DIRECT speech form of the indirect sentence:
He told me that he had been waiting for me since morning.

options.option_text: He said to me, 'I was waiting for you since morning.'
He said to me, 'I have been waiting for you since morning.'
He said to me, 'I had been waiting for you since morning.'
He said to me, 'I am waiting for you since morning.'

questions.explanation: B is correct. Reverse backshift: Past Perfect Continuous ('had been waiting') → Present Perfect Continuous ('have been waiting') in direct speech. Past Perfect Continuous in indirect speech comes from Present Perfect Continuous in direct speech. 'Since morning' stays unchanged (it's a specific time reference, not a relative time expression).

questions.stem:
Convert to indirect speech:
She said, 'I wish I could speak French fluently.'

options.option_text: She said that she wished she can speak French fluently.
She said that she wished she could speak French fluently.
She said that she wishes she could speak French fluently.
She said that she had wished she could speak French fluently.

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Wish' + 'could' (past modal) — modal verbs like 'could', 'would', 'should', 'might', 'ought to' do NOT change in indirect speech (they are already past forms). Only non-past modals change: will→would, can→could, may→might. 'I wish I could' → 'she wished she could' (only 'wish' backshifts to 'wished'; 'could' stays unchanged).
